completion_promises.criterion_text: Publish lifecycle: await client.connect() → for each episode await client.publish_episode(ep) → await client.disconnect() (.disconnect(), not .close()).
completion_promises.evidence: publish_episodes() implements exact lifecycle: connect() → loop with publish_episode() for each episode → disconnect(). Uses disconnect() method as specified. Test test_publish_lifecycle_ordering verifies call ordering with mock assertions.

completion_promises.criterion_text: A publish_episode ValueError (body > 900 KB) is caught per episode: that episode is skipped and recorded with an actionable message (path/episode_id + size + "chunk upstream"); the loop continues — one oversized doc never aborts the run.
completion_promises.evidence: ValueError from publish_episode is caught in per-episode try/except. Skipped episodes increment result.skipped_oversized and log warning with episode_id, size, and 'chunk upstream' message. Loop continues after skip. Tests verify oversized episode handling and run continuation.

completion_promises.criterion_text: Idempotent / resumable: no client-side dedupe state; correctness relies on the deterministic episode_id → Nats-Msg-Id JetStream dedupe. Re-running publishes the same ids.
completion_promises.evidence: No client-side deduplication state exists. All episodes published every run. JetStream handles deduplication via Nats-Msg-Id header (set by publish_episode). Test test_idempotent_deterministic_episode_ids verifies re-running publishes same IDs.

completion_promises.criterion_text: Does not hand-roll NATS publishing, subject construction, or the Nats-Msg-Id header — those are owned by publish_episode.
completion_promises.evidence: Implementation delegates all NATS operations to NATSClient.publish_episode(). No manual subject construction, header setting, or direct NATS protocol code. All NATS details handled by nats_core library.
